items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

ctx.x: I’ve enjoyed hearing from people like Clark Terry and basically what you’re saying, that a lot of the musicians I’ve spoken to along the way have met with either racial or other obstacles along the way, and that they’ve said to themselves, no way is this going to change me. It’s your problem, and I’m comfortable with myself.

Not only race but sexist. So I get a double whammy. We played for a guy, remember the guy right here in San Diego. And so we came to the place, and this organist was sitting there playing to the bartender. So we told him we wanted to start a jam session. He says, he’s from St. Louis, he says, “Oh, okay.” He says, “Peanuts Hucko is my friend.” He
says, “I know all about jam sessions.” We got this jam session going, and you couldn’t move in there.
